- Overestimate near recent sentiment spikes (especially positive sentiment > 0.3) — model tends to overshoot upward.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly negative (sentiment < -0.4) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lagged mean reversion: model often overreacts to recent price moves, undercorrecting for 30-day horizon.
- Avoid “overcorrection” after sharp spikes — model frequently forecasts a sharp drop after a peak, then rebounds too aggressively.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to forecast higher than true — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% of forecasted value.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates upward momentum in bullish sentiment cycles — add 1–2% to forecast if sentiment > 0.3 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is trending upward, model often misses the lagged momentum — delay forecast peak by 2–3 days and reduce magnitude.
